pairs.title: Local topology, entropy compactness and path-space estimates

A.title: Local topologies
A.statement: For a finite nonempty alphabet S, equip S^(Z^d) with the product topology and cylinder sigma algebra; local convergence is convergence of every finite-coordinate marginal.
A.proof_route: Explicit weighted cylinder metric and diagonal subsequence construction.

A.title: Finite chain martingale
A.statement: For a finite matrix L with nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums, bounded real f and every initial law, M_t=f(X_t)-f(X_0)-integral_0^t Lf(X_s)ds is square integrable with bracket integral_0^t (L(f²)-2fLf)(X_s)ds.
A.proof_route: Derive conditional expectation by e^(tL), then apply the product increment identity; reversibility is unnecessary.

A.title: Finite doob bound
A.statement: Every square-integrable cadlag martingale M with M_0=0 obeys E sup_(t<=T)|M_t|²<=4 E|M_T|².
A.proof_route: Stopping on first crossing, tail integration with truncation and Cauchy–Schwarz; take monotone limits.

A.title: Finite entropy chain
A.statement: For finite joint laws P,Q with Q positive, D(P||Q)=D(P_X||Q_X)+sum_x P_X(x)D(P_(Y|x)||Q_(Y|x)); grouping events decreases relative entropy.
A.proof_route: Expand logarithmic ratio, omit zero P atoms, and use log-sum inequality.

B.title: Singular local limit
B.statement: A sequence of fixed-label particles can converge trivially locally while a spatially selected particle has a nontrivial mark law.
B.proof_route: Use uniform particles on expanding boxes; fixed label enters a fixed box with probability tending to zero.

pairs.title: Quantitative DLR uniqueness, concentration and spatial response

A.title: Dobrushin matrix
A.statement: For a finite-spin specification, c_ij is the maximal total variation change of the i conditional law after changing only spin j; C has zero diagonal.
A.proof_route: Finite kernels and finite supremum; define infinite boundary supremum explicitly.

A.title: Dobrushin comparison
A.statement: If C has nonnegative entries and row sums <=c<1, two Gibbs measures with conditional discrepancies bounded by b satisfy |mu f-nu f|<=sum_i delta_i(f)[(I-C)^(-1)b]_i for every bounded cylinder f.
A.proof_route: Finite-volume coupled update stationary law; solve disagreement inequality by nonnegative Neumann series; pass cylinder limits.

A.title: High temperature susceptibility
A.statement: For translation-invariant finite-range Ising kernels with the uniform Dobrushin row bound c<1 on an open parameter interval, bounded-spin correlations are absolutely summable and the limiting magnetization derivative is the covariance sum.
A.proof_route: Distance support of powers C^n yields geometric tail; differentiate finite volume then uniformly control tails.

B.title: Ising explicit contraction
B.statement: Nearest-neighbor Ising on Z^d has c_ij<=tanh(beta |J_ij|); 2d tanh(beta |J|)<1 is sufficient for the comparison theorem.
B.proof_route: Compute the two Bernoulli conditional laws and maximize their difference; the bound is sufficient, not the exact critical temperature.

pairs.title: Polymer analyticity and dilute continuum correlations

A.title: Abstract polymer
A.statement: An abstract polymer model is a countable set with reflexive symmetric incompatibility, activities z, and finite-volume partition function given by compatible subsets.
A.proof_route: Finite polynomial definition; no convergence assertion in definition.

A.title: Polymer tree majorant
A.statement: Under sum_(eta incompatible gamma)|z_eta|exp(a_eta)<=a_gamma, the absolute rooted connected-cluster sum with root gamma is bounded by exp(a_gamma).
A.proof_route: Prove connected-graph cancellation/tree partition and iterate rooted-tree generating series monotonically; display multiplicity factorials.

A.title: Polymer analyticity
A.statement: A strict locally uniform polymer majorant implies a zero-free finite partition function and normally convergent connected expansion for log Z in that activity domain.
A.proof_route: Start near zero with the formal exponential formula, apply normal convergence and analytic continuation within the star-shaped majorant domain.

A.title: Stable mayer tree bound
A.statement: For a measurable stable translation-invariant pair potential v on R^d with stability constant B, beta>0 and finite C_beta=integral_R^d |exp(-beta v)-1|, pin x_1=0. For n>=2 the integral over x_2,...,x_n of the absolute connected-graph Mayer sum is at most exp(2 beta B n)n^(n-2) C_beta^(n-1).
A.proof_route: Prove a stability-preserving graph-to-tree partition and integrate tree leaves; full local proof required before corollary dispatch.

A.title: Dilute mayer domain
A.statement: The stable regular continuum pressure Mayer series converges absolutely when |z|exp(2 beta B+1) C_beta<1, with termwise activity derivatives on compact subdomains.
A.proof_route: Apply coefficient bound, n! growth and uniform ratio majorant; identify finite-volume coefficients by dominated boundary-to-volume limit.

B.title: Hard core dilute bound
B.statement: For hard spheres of diameter a, B=0 and C_beta is the ball volume of radius a, so e |z| C_beta<1 is an explicit sufficient analytic domain.
B.proof_route: Mayer function is minus the exclusion-ball indicator; this is a sufficient bound rather than a freezing prediction.

pairs.title: Large-deviation variational mechanics and ensemble inequivalence

A.title: Compact laplace tilt
A.statement: If X_n has an LDP with rate I on compact K and F is continuous, the log-Laplace limit is sup_K(F-I), and normalized exp(nF) tilting gives rate I-F+sup_K(F-I).
A.proof_route: Finite cover upper estimate and open neighborhood lower estimate; establish both LDP bounds of tilted laws.

A.title: Mean field supporting lines
A.statement: For finite alphabet p>0 and continuous h, canonical macrostates minimize D(q||p)+beta h(q); a constrained macrostate at energy u is canonical at beta precisely when it minimizes the constrained entropy cost and u maximizes s(v)-beta v.
A.proof_route: Contraction on compact simplex and the two minimizations; microcanonical claim uses explicitly matched shrinking-window infima.

A.title: Curie weiss bifurcation
A.statement: For J>0 and H=0 the Curie–Weiss canonical magnetization minimizer is uniquely zero when beta J<=1 and consists of +/-m_beta when beta J>1, where m_beta is the unique positive solution m=tanh(beta Jm).
A.proof_route: Differentiate binary entropy, prove atanh(m)/m strictly increasing from 1 to infinity; inspect derivative signs and boundary continuity.

B.title: Nonexposed energy
B.statement: For a binary uniform reference and mean-field energy h(q)=q_1^(1/4), the constrained entropy s(u)=H_binary(u^4)-log 2 is strictly convex for 0<u<=1/10. These interior energies are not canonical equilibrium energies for any inverse temperature.
B.proof_route: The constraint uniquely fixes q_1=u^4. Compute s second derivative =u²[12 log((1-u^4)/u^4)-16/(1-u^4)], strictly positive on (0,1/10]. A locally strictly convex function cannot lie below a supporting affine line at an interior point; apply supporting-line criterion.

pairs.title: Criticality, Gaussian fields and exact block renormalization

A.title: Gaussian lattice
A.statement: For finite periodic lattice and m²,kappa>0 define K=m²I+kappa(-Delta) and the Gaussian probability with precision K.
A.proof_route: Positive Fourier symbol and Gaussian integral.

A.title: Gaussian massless dimension
A.statement: The infinite-lattice Fourier integral for massless covariance at fixed separation is finite in d>2 and its diagonal diverges in d<=2.
A.proof_route: Bound sum sin²(k_i/2) above/below by constants times |k|² near zero and use radial integrability.

A.title: Gaussian block rg
A.statement: Input a finite positive definite precision matrix and an ordered finite list of retained-coordinate subsets. At each step permute retained coordinates first, partition into A,B,C, solve C X=B^T and output A-BX plus the exact log-determinant normalization increment; terminate after the list.
A.proof_route: Procedure only; exact arithmetic contract and nonsingular eliminated principal blocks.

A.title: Gaussian block rg correct
A.statement: The block-RG procedure terminates after its finite list and returns the exact retained Gaussian marginals and normalization factors.
A.proof_route: Complete square, prove Schur complement positive using the minimizing quadratic form, then induct on list length.

A.title: Quartic engineering scaling
A.statement: For smooth compactly supported fields under x=b xprime and phi(x)=b^(-(d-2)/2) phi_prime(xprime), the gradient action is invariant and the quartic coefficient transforms by b^(4-d).
A.proof_route: Direct change of variables and chain rule, no interacting measure asserted.

B.title: Rg generates couplings
B.statement: Eliminating the center of a Gaussian star creates couplings between all remaining leaves.
B.proof_route: For nonzero central-to-leaf entries, off-diagonal Schur correction is -b_i b_j/C.

pairs.title: Classical Potts random clusters and planar loop transfer

A.title: Finite potts fk
A.statement: For finite graph, integer Q>=2 and nonnegative v_e, define spin weights and random-cluster weights Q^k(A) product_e v_e with their finite positive normalizers.
A.proof_route: Finite sums; zero activities allowed.

A.title: Edwards sokal
A.statement: The component-coloring joint law has the Potts and FK marginals and satisfies P(sigma_x=sigma_y)=1/Q+(1-1/Q)P(x connected y).
A.proof_route: Expand edge factors and count Q choices per connected component; condition on connection event.

A.title: Fk connectivity transfer
A.statement: Input a finite ordered strip graph, Q>=2 and v_e>=0; start from empty connectivity, process each edge by identity plus v_e times join, detach vertices after their final edge multiplying by Q on closed components, then sum terminal weights.
A.proof_route: Specify deterministic edge ordering and component closure rule.

A.title: Fk transfer correct
A.statement: The connectivity transfer terminates after finitely many edges and returns Z_FK exactly in exact arithmetic.
A.proof_route: Induct on processed-edge subsets, track live partition and already closed cluster factor; final detach accounts for every component exactly once.

A.title: Classical medial loop normalization
A.statement: For a finite connected planar graph with specified free exterior boundary, the FK partition polynomial can be rewritten as a medial noncrossing-loop sum with loop value sqrt(Q), with the graph-dependent Euler prefactor and edge weights explicitly retained.
A.proof_route: For each edge subset use planar Euler k(A)-k(Astar)=|V|-|A|-1 and number of medial loops k(A)+k(Astar)-1. Hence Q^k(A) v^|A|=Q^(|V|/2) (sqrt(Q))^loops product_(e in A)(v_e/sqrt(Q)), under the convention that boundary loops count the exterior component once. Verify the single-edge and empty connected graph cases; derive before transfer use.

B.title: Potts two vertices
B.statement: For a single edge the FK normalizer is Q²+Qv and the same-color probability is (1+v)/(Q+v).
B.proof_route: Enumerate empty and occupied edge subsets and verify direct spin count.

pairs.title: Diffusive hydrodynamics from the symmetric exclusion process

A.title: Ssep diffusive model
A.statement: Define SSEP on (Z/NZ)^d by nearest-neighbor unordered-bond swaps at rate N², with empirical measure N^(-d)sum eta_x delta_(x/N).
A.proof_route: Finite generator; rate scaling and occupation-conserving state sectors explicit.

A.title: Ssep bracket
A.statement: For smooth periodic G, the empirical-field martingale drift is <pi,Delta_N G> and its bracket on [0,T] is bounded by C_G T N^(-d).
A.proof_route: Compute each bond jump, square, sum rates and use gradient bound.

A.title: Ssep heat limit
A.statement: If initial empirical measures converge in probability to rho_0 dx with 0<=rho_0<=1, then for every smooth periodic G and T finite, sup_(t<=T)|<pi_t^N,G>-integral rho_t G| tends to zero in probability, where rho_t is the heat solution with datum rho_0.
A.proof_route: Backward heat test, bracket estimate, Fourier heat construction, uniform Laplacian consistency and time mesh; author heat construction locally in proof.

B.title: Ssep density mode
B.statement: An initial density rho_0(x)=a+b cos(2pi k.x), with |b|<=min(a,1-a), evolves as a+b exp(-4pi²|k|²t) cos(2pi k.x).
B.proof_route: Fourier diagonalization; these are density predictions conditional on SSEP, not measured diffusion.

pairs.title: Hydrodynamic fluctuation action and nonequilibrium quasipotential

A.title: Ssep current action
A.statement: For smooth periodic rho in [epsilon,1-epsilon] and j satisfying continuity, define I(rho,j;0,T)=one quarter integral |j+grad rho|²/[rho(1-rho)].
A.proof_route: Admissible smooth paths and fixed positive epsilon ensure finite integrand.

A.title: Mft reversal identity
A.statement: For the smooth admissible paths, I(rho,j)-I(theta rho,-theta j)=integral f(rho_T)-integral f(rho_0), where theta reverses time and f(r)=r log r+(1-r)log(1-r).
A.proof_route: Expand squares, substitute f second derivative, use periodic integration by parts and continuity.

A.title: Equilibrium quasipotential
A.statement: For smooth strictly interior target rho on a torus with mean rbar in (0,1), the infinite-horizon action infimum from homogeneous rbar is integral [rho log(rho/rbar)+(1-rho)log((1-rho)/(1-rbar))].
A.proof_route: Reversal identity gives lower bound; reverse heat relaxation, smooth positive bounds and limiting small initial correction give upper bound; state limiting horizon precisely.

B.title: Mft nonlocal warning
B.statement: For two-site SSEP with bond swap rate 1, left insertion/removal rates alpha,1-alpha and right rates beta,1-beta, where alpha,beta are in (0,1), the stationary occupation covariance is -(alpha-beta)^2/18. The stationary law is not a product when alpha differs from beta.
B.proof_route: Stationarity gives m_1=(2alpha+beta)/3 and m_2=(alpha+2beta)/3, and L(eta_1 eta_2)=alpha eta_2+beta eta_1-2eta_1 eta_2. Thus E product=(alpha m_2+beta m_1)/2; subtract m_1m_2. This is a finite correlation example, not a derivation of the continuum quasipotential.

pairs.title: Kinetic relaxation, diffusive scaling and entropy dissipation

A.title: Two velocity scaling
A.statement: On the periodic line define two-velocity transport with speeds +/-c/epsilon, turning rate lambda/epsilon², c,lambda>0, and nonnegative smooth initial densities.
A.proof_route: Explicit linear periodic PDE and scaling parameters.

A.title: Two velocity contraction
A.statement: The two-velocity evolution preserves nonnegativity and mass and contracts the L² norm of the pair.
A.proof_route: Positive transport/turning semigroup by finite alternating-step limit; multiply PDEs by f and integrate, dissipation -(2lambda/epsilon²)norm(f_plus-f_minus)².

A.title: Two velocity heat limit
A.statement: For smooth well-prepared periodic initial data f_plus=f_minus=rho_0/2, rho^epsilon converges in L² uniformly on bounded time intervals to heat evolution with D=c²/(2lambda).
A.proof_route: Solve each Fourier 2x2 mode, show fixed-mode uniform convergence including initial layer amplitude, then control tails by contraction.

B.title: Distinct scaling limits
B.statement: Mean-field N^(-1) interaction, hard-sphere Boltzmann–Grad N a^(d-1) fixed and two-velocity diffusive scaling are distinct model limits.
B.proof_route: Write dimensions and conserved quantities for each; this is a comparison, not mutual implication.

pairs.title: Path entropy production, fluctuation symmetry and work identities

A.title: Stationary path entropy
A.statement: For finite irreducible q with symmetric support and invariant pi>0, define S_T as the sum over jumps of log[pi_x q_xy/(pi_y q_yx)] for a stationary path.
A.proof_route: Permit nonreversible q explicitly; finite rates and finite T imply nonexplosion.

A.title: Finite path fluctuation
A.statement: The stationary path and its time reversal have likelihood ratio exp(S_T); E exp(-S_T)=1 and P(S_T in ds)=exp(s)P(S_T in -ds).
A.proof_route: Write ordered jump-time densities for every number of jumps, cancel holding factors, telescope pi, then push forward by S.

A.title: Finite jarzynski
A.statement: For finite energies E_x(t) of class C^1 on [0,T], beta>0, finite bounded continuous jump rates with instantaneous Gibbs detailed balance and initial law pi_0, define W=integral_0^T partial_t E_(X_t)(t)dt and Z_t=sum_x exp(-beta E_x(t)). Then E exp(-beta W)=Z_T/Z_0.
A.proof_route: Prove finite Feynman–Kac ODE; weighted law g_x(t)=exp(-beta E_x(t))/Z_0 solves it exactly.

B.title: Biased ring entropy
B.statement: For a homogeneous ring with clockwise rate a>0 and counterclockwise rate b>0, stationary pi is uniform and S_T=(N_clock-N_counter)log(a/b).
B.proof_route: Compute jump product and mean entropy production (a-b)log(a/b)>=0; reversibility iff a=b.

pairs.title: Gibbs sampling, exact coupling and finite-error certificates

A.title: Heat bath update
A.statement: Input finite positive Gibbs weights, initial configuration and integer t>=0. Repeat t times: choose a site uniformly, draw independent U uniform on [0,1], and replace that spin by the first cumulative conditional interval containing U. Output final configuration.
A.proof_route: Operational definition; half-open intervals and last-interval U=1 convention.

A.title: Heat bath tv bound
A.statement: For n sites and Dobrushin row and column sums bounded by c<1, the random-scan heat-bath chain has worst-start TV distance <=n exp(-(1-c)t/n).
A.proof_route: Maximal site couplings and Hamming expected contraction; column bound is explicit to justify unweighted Hamming norm.

A.title: Monotone cftp
A.statement: Input ferromagnetic finite Ising model and a stored iid site/uniform stream indexed by negative integers; replay common updates from all-minus and all-plus from horizons -1,-2,-4,...; stop when outputs agree and return that common state.
A.proof_route: Store and reuse seeds on overlaps; no resampling old randomness.

A.title: Monotone cftp exact
A.statement: With finite positive Ising heat-bath conditionals and finite sites, monotone CFTP terminates almost surely and its output has exactly the Gibbs law.
A.proof_route: Monotonicity, positive finite forcing block, probability-one coalescence, then sandwich a stationary chain coupled from the same past.

A.title: Swendsen wang
A.statement: For integer Q>=2 ferromagnetic finite Potts weights, activate each equal-spin edge independently with probability v_e/(1+v_e), then recolor each bond component independently uniformly in Q colors.
A.proof_route: Two explicit conditional draws.

A.title: Swendsen wang invariance
A.statement: The Swendsen–Wang procedure preserves the finite Potts Gibbs law; it terminates after finite bond and component operations.
A.proof_route: Composition of Edwards–Sokal conditional kernels preserves the joint law and hence spin marginal; no efficiency claim.

B.title: Metastable diagnostic
B.statement: A finite low-temperature chain can appear stationary within one phase while its worst-start mixing time is large.
B.proof_route: Use a two-well finite energy model; compute bottleneck exit probability and show diagnostic failure is compatible with exact invariance.

pairs.title: Inverse Gibbs models, identifiability and correlated uncertainty

A.title: Inverse finite exponential
A.statement: For finite X, positive reference weights and statistic T:X->R^k, define A(theta)=log sum_x w(x)exp(theta.T(x)) and the normalized Gibbs family.
A.proof_route: Finite normalization positive everywhere.

A.title: Inverse identifiability
A.statement: The Hessian of A is Cov_theta(T), and it is positive definite for every theta iff no nonzero linear combination of T is constant on X.
A.proof_route: Differentiate finite sums; a variance vanishes iff the variable is constant on the full positive support.

A.title: Finite mle existence
A.statement: In a minimal finite exponential family the iid MLE is finite and unique precisely when the sample sufficient-statistic mean lies in the relative interior of conv(T(X)).
A.proof_route: Interior supplies coercivity of A(theta)-theta.Tbar by a compact unit-sphere separation bound; boundary exposes a direction with positive derivative preventing finite maximum.

A.title: Latent gibbs observation
A.statement: A latent Gibbs observation model consists of a proper prior on theta, finite Gibbs state pi_theta and a probability kernel K(y|sigma,theta); its likelihood is sum_sigma pi_theta(sigma)K(y|sigma,theta).
A.proof_route: Specify measured datum and latent configuration separately.

A.title: Inverse posterior
A.statement: For the latent Gibbs model on standard-Borel parameter/data spaces with proper prior, a posterior kernel exists under AC and is unique only prior-predictive almost everywhere.
A.proof_route: Apply exact posterior supplier hypotheses; dominated positive likelihood gives Bayes formula only where normalizer is finite positive.

B.title: Boundary mle
B.statement: All-plus iid observations in a Bernoulli spin family have no finite field MLE; the likelihood increases toward field +infinity.
B.proof_route: Sufficient mean is an exposed endpoint; differentiate logistic log likelihood.

pairs.title: Planar random clusters, sharpness and the exact square-lattice critical point

A.title: Fk real boundaries
A.statement: For real q>=1, p in (0,1), finite graph and boundary partition xi, define FK mass proportional to p^o(1-p)^c q^(k after wiring xi).
A.proof_route: Finite positive normalization; real q extension independent of spin coloring.

A.title: Fk fkg spatial markov
A.statement: Finite FK with q>=1 is positively associated, satisfies the spatial Markov property, and is stochastically increasing in p and boundary wiring.
A.proof_route: Prove supermodular component count, finite lattice-condition induction, exact conditioned edge weights and monotone single-edge coupling.

A.title: Fk planar duality
A.statement: On a finite planar graph with dual boundary convention, complementing edges sends FK(p,q) to dual FK(pstar,q), where pstar/(1-pstar)=q(1-p)/p.
A.proof_route: Euler formula with exterior face and wired/free swap; retain explicit partition normalization prefactor.

A.title: Fk torus rsw
A.statement: For q>=1 and fixed alpha>1, at p_sd=sqrt(q)/(1+sqrt(q)) there is c(alpha,q)>0 such that every admissible rectangle of side alpha n by n in a periodic square torus of side m>alpha n has horizontal crossing probability at least c(alpha,q).
A.proof_route: Source Theorem 5: square bound from self-duality, exploration/reflection gluing Lemma 7, aspect enlargement Proposition 8, iterate; retain periodic boundary throughout.

A.title: Fk influence threshold
A.statement: For fixed q>=1 and epsilon>0, a finite FK model with p in [epsilon,1-epsilon] and any increasing event A has an edge e with I_A(e)=P(A|omega_e=1)-P(A|omega_e=0) at least c(q,epsilon)P(A)(1-P(A))log(|E|)/|E| for |E|>=2.
A.proof_route: Full missing local proof follows the source Theorem 12 and its cited monotone-measure influence argument; source Sections 3–4 alone state the deepest input, so author the finite revealment/entropy estimate rather than treating the citation as proof.

A.title: Fk crossing amplification
A.statement: For q>=1, periodic crossing estimates at p_sd, the FK differential influence inequality and boundary monotonicity imply percolation for p>p_sd and exponential two-point decay for p<p_sd on Z².
A.proof_route: Source Section 4: symmetric torus sharp threshold, wired rectangle amplification, boundary-aware path concatenation, then subcritical moment and finite-size decay bounds. Explicitly author the concatenation and decay subarguments before use.

A.title: Fk square critical point
A.statement: For every real q>=1 the square-lattice FK threshold is p_c=sqrt(q)/(1+sqrt(q)); below p_c every infinite-volume FK state has two-point connectivity bounded by C(p,q)exp(-c(p,q)|x-y|).
A.proof_route: Combine both sides of threshold and free/wired comparison; do not infer behavior at p_c.

A.title: Potts square critical temperature
A.statement: For integer Q>=2 and square-lattice Potts energy -J sum_edge delta_spin with J>0, the critical inverse temperature obeys beta_c J=log(1+sqrt(Q)).
A.proof_route: Set p=1-exp(-beta J), use wired order/connectivity identity and monotonic thermodynamic limits.

B.title: Ising coupling conversion
B.statement: Square-lattice zero-field Ising with energy -J sum sigma_x sigma_y has beta_c J=log(1+sqrt(2))/2.
B.proof_route: Use delta_(sigma_x=sigma_y)=(1+sigma_x sigma_y)/2, retaining the constant energy shift.

pairs.title: Rare-event reweighting, overlap and certified partition ratios

A.title: Partition ratio overlap
A.statement: For positive weights on a finite space and iid pi_0 samples, the sample mean of w_1/w_0 is unbiased for Z_1/Z_0 and its relative variance is chi²(pi_1||pi_0)/n.
A.proof_route: Finite change of measure, normalize R by Z_1/Z_0, compute its second moment exactly.

A.title: Independent bridge ratios
A.statement: Input positive finite weights w_0,...,w_K and independent stages of n_k>=1 iid exact pi_k draws; compute each mean w_(k+1)/w_k and return their product.
A.proof_route: K finite; no approximate Gibbs samples accepted by this exact contract.

A.title: Bridge ratio variance
A.statement: The independent bridge-ratio output is unbiased for Z_K/Z_0 and its relative second moment equals product_k[1+chi²(pi_(k+1)||pi_k)/n_k].
A.proof_route: Stage independence factors expectations and second moments; use overlap theorem for each.

A.title: Interval finite partition
A.statement: Input a finite enumerated configuration space, finite rational intervals enclosing every strictly positive weight, and finite observable intervals. Add and multiply by outward-rounded interval operations, then divide observable-weight sum by partition interval only if its lower bound is positive; otherwise return unresolved denominator.
A.proof_route: Exact finite enumeration and defined failure branch; no unprovided exponential primitive.

A.title: Interval partition certificate
A.statement: The interval finite-partition procedure terminates and encloses the exact Z and, on successful division, the exact normalized expectation for every admissible input weight and observable choice.
A.proof_route: Induct on finite expression DAG using actual enclosure theorem; failure branch asserts no ratio enclosure.

B.title: Product overlap explosion
B.statement: If pi_0 and pi_1 are distinct positive iid product laws on n coordinates, then 1+chi²(pi_1||pi_0)=(1+chi²(one-site target||one-site reference))^n.
B.proof_route: Factor finite second-moment sum coordinate by coordinate; prove exponential overlap cost for fixed distinct one-site laws.
